judgments.explanation: The mention 阮光禄 refers to a person surnamed Ruan holding the Guanglu office, who is the interlocutor with 謝安 in the narrative. Candidate c0 (謝安) is a distinct person in the same narrative, not the referent. Candidate c1 (孫龍) appears in the Liu annotation discussing the 'White Horse' paradox (白馬非馬) attributed to Gongsun Long, but there is no evidence linking 孫龍 to the person surnamed Ruan holding Guanglu office. Candidate c2 (裕) appears in the annotation fragment '中興書曰裕' but there is insufficient evidence to connect this to 阮光禄. None of the supplied candidates is supported as the historical referent of 阮光禄.

The mention 字景真 is the courtesy name of 桓亮 (Huan Liang). The Liu annotation explicitly states 續晉陽秋曰桓亮字景真 (sfh1-ev-19-xianyuan-032-liu-annotation-003), directly identifying 桓亮 as the person whose courtesy name is 景真. The main text also refers to this person as 桓景真 (sfh1-ev-19-xianyuan-032-main), and the annotation further identifies 亮 as the one who killed 韓繪之 (sfh1-ev-19-xianyuan-032-liu-annotation-004). Candidate c7 (桓亮) is the direct referent. Candidate c8 (桓景真) is the same person referenced by name+courtesy name combination, and c2 (亮) is the short form of the same person's given name. The preferred candidate is c7 (桓亮) as the canonical historical person.

The mention 謝豫章 refers to Xie Kun (謝鯤), who held the office of Yuzhang (豫章) administrator. The main text states '謝仁祖年八嵗謝豫章將送客' — Xie Renzu (Xie Shang) at age 8, with Xie Yuzhang being his father. The Liu annotation-001 explicitly notes '(别見/鯤子)' identifying the subject as Kun's son, and annotation-002 states '人鯤之子也' (son of Kun). The reference semantics indicate this is an office-holder reference where 豫章 designates Xie Kun, who served as Yuzhang administrator. Candidate c0 (謝鯤) is the correct referent. Candidates c1 (温嶠), c3 (尚), c4 (嶠) appear in annotation-003 as different persons in the narrative about Xie Shang's mourning. Candidate c2 (謝尚) is the son, distinct from the father referenced by 謝豫章. Candidate c5 (顔回) is a different person mentioned in the main text.

The mention '齊桓公' refers to Duke Huan of Qi, the ruler whom Guan Zhong (管仲/管夷吾) served. The main text mentions '管夷吾' (Guan Yiwu, i.e., Guan Zhong) in the context of the Jiangdong region having its own Guan Yiwu. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-02-yanyu-036-liu-annotation-001) explicitly states '管仲夷吾者潁上人相齊桓公' — Guan Zhong Yiwu served Duke Huan of Qi. The annotation (sfh1-ev-02-yanyu-036-liu-annotation-003) also references '管仲' in connection with the same exemplum. Candidates c2 (管仲), c3 (管仲夷吾), and c4 (管夷吾) all refer to the same historical person Guan Zhong, who served Duke Huan of Qi. The mention '齊桓公' is the ruler, not Guan Zhong himself. However, since the candidates c2, c3, c4 all denote Guan Zhong (the person who served Duke Huan), and the mention refers to Duke Huan of Qi as the ruler whom Guan Zhong served, the candidates are all the same historical person Guan Zhong. The most direct match is c4 (管夷吾) which appears in the main text and is explicitly identified in the annotation as the one who '相齊桓公' (served as minister to Duke Huan of Qi). Candidates c0 (劉琨) and c1 (温嶠) are figures from the main narrative (Wen Jiao served as Liu Kun's envoy), not the historical exemplum referent Duke Huan of Qi. The mention '齊桓公' is the ruler of Qi, and the candidates provided are Guan Zhong (the minister), so the resolution is that the candidate Guan Zhong (管夷吾/管仲) is the person associated with the mention context — the annotation identifies Guan Zhong as serving Duke Huan of Qi. Given the candidates all denote Guan Zhong, and the mention is Duke Huan of Qi, the best-supported candidate is c4 (管夷吾) as it appears directly in the main text and is explicitly linked to 齊桓公 in the annotation.

The Liu annotation explicitly states '謙字敬祖' (謙's courtesy name is 敬祖), directly identifying the mention 敬祖 as referring to 桓謙. Candidate c2 (桓謙) is supported by this explicit annotation. Candidate c5 (謙) is also supported as the same person referenced by the shortened name 謙 in the annotation. Candidate c0 (卞範之) is contradicted because 卞範之's courtesy name is 敬祖 per the external evidence, but the annotation here explicitly assigns 敬祖 to 謙, not 卞範之. Candidate c3 (殷仲文) is contradicted because the main text distinguishes 桓謙 from 殷仲文 as separate people. Candidates c1 (仲文) and c4 (沖) lack direct evidence linking them to the mention 敬祖.

The mention '主簿' (chief clerk) refers to 何充. The main text states '時何充爲敦主簿' (at that time He Chong was Dun's chief clerk), explicitly identifying the 主簿 as 何充. The Liu annotation confirms this with '主簿充知敦有異志' (chief clerk Chong knew Dun had different intentions). The patron is 王敦 (敦), not the referent. 沈充, 王敦, 含有惠政, and 王含 are all different persons and do not match the office-holder reference.

The surface 桓宣武 refers to 桓溫, who held the title/designation 宣武. Candidate c0 (桓溫) is directly supported by the canonical registry evidence (registry:person-008), the biographical entry (evidence-p3b-wave-1-f59e4cdd4d2bf2b6878f7d72) confirming 桓溫's identity, and the main text evidence (evidence-p3b-wave-1-2d7e5c33cdd9167acbe1f5dc) where 桓宣武 is used for 桓溫. The main text (sfh1-ev-25-paidiao-026-main) shows 謝公 serving as 桓宣武's 司馬, consistent with 桓溫. Candidates c1 (謝安/安石) is the 謝公 in the text, not the referent. c2 (傅先正), c3 (桓玄), and c4 (髙靈) appear in annotations or as other persons in the text, not as the referent of 桓宣武.

The mention 車騎 refers to the person holding the office title of General of Chariots and Cavalry. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-02-yanyu-078-liu-annotation-003) glosses 玄字㓜度鎭西 and 謝車騎家傳曰, identifying 車騎 as 謝玄 (courtesy name 㓜度). Candidate c0 (謝玄) is the correct referent. Candidate c3 (㓜度) is the courtesy name of the same person, and c5 (玄) is the given name of the same person, so they also refer to 謝玄. Candidates c1 (山濤) and c2 (謝安) are different persons in the text, and c4 (奕) is a different person mentioned in the annotation.

The mention '桓' at position 11-12 in the main text refers to 桓子野 (Huan Ziye), the flute player. The main text says '遇桓於岸上過' — encountering Huan passing on the shore — referring back to 桓子野 introduced earlier in the same text. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-23-rendan-049-liu-annotation-002) identifies this person as 桓伊 (Huan Yi), the general who was skilled at music. 桓子野 is the courtesy name (字) of 桓伊. Both c2 (桓伊) and c3 (桓子野) refer to the same historical person. c0 (謝安) is a different person mentioned in the annotation as present at the banquet. c4 (王子猷) is the other main character in the story, not the referent of this mention. c1 (伊) is an abbreviated form from the annotation, insufficient on its own. The preferred candidate is c2 (桓伊) as the full historical name.

The mention 殷荆州 refers to the person surnamed 殷 who held the office of governor of Jingzhou (荆州). The main text (sfh1-ev-06-yaliang-041-main) shows 殷 as the actor in the narrative, and the reference semantics identify this as 殷仲堪. Candidate c0 (殷仲堪) matches the referent hint and the office-holder reference. Candidates c1 (束晳), c2 (王恭), c3 (孟達), c4 (晳), and c5 (踈廣) are all different persons mentioned in the text or annotations, not the referent of 殷荆州.

The mention 劉尹 refers to a person identified by surname 劉 plus office title 尹 (governor/administrator). The main text shows 劉尹 visiting 禇 together with 王長史. None of the supplied candidates clearly matches this office-holder reference. 何充 (c0) is 驃騎 (referenced as 何驃騎 in the text), not 劉尹. 劉惔 (c1) is referred to as 真長 in the text, not 劉尹. 劉遐 (c2) is 吏部尚書, a different office. 沈充 (c3) is 充, not 劉尹. 王胡之 (c4) and 裒 (c5) are annotation figures with insufficient evidence connecting them to the 劉尹 office title. The reference semantics note that 劉尹 is distinct from 劉遐. Without a candidate who is specifically identified as holding the 尹 office with surname 劉, no candidate can be supported.

The mention '武子' refers to 王武子 (Wang Wuzi), whose personal name was 王濟 (Wang Ji). The main text (sfh1-ev-05-fangzheng-011-main) explicitly names 王武子 as the person the emperor discusses, and the Liu annotations (sfh1-ev-05-fangzheng-011-liu-annotation-001, -002, -003) identify 王濟 as the same person. Candidate c5 (王濟) is the most fully supported identification, with c4 (王武子) and c3 (濟) also referring to the same individual. Candidates c0 (和嶠), c1 (王戎), c6 (瓉), and c7 (甄德) are different people mentioned in the same passage.

The mention 嚴仲弼 refers to the person whose given name is 仲弼 and surname 嚴. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-08-shangyu-020-liu-annotation-005) states '仲弼吳郡人...嚴隱字' which identifies 嚴隱 as having the courtesy name 仲弼. Thus 嚴仲弼 = 嚴隱 (courtesy name 仲弼). Candidate c2 (仲弼) and c5 (嚴隱) both refer to this same person. The main text mentions 嚴仲弼 as one of the Wu worthies. The annotation confirms 嚴隱字仲弼. Both c2 and c5 are supported, but c2 (仲弼) directly matches the surface 嚴仲弼's given name component. The preferred candidate is c2.

The mention 宣王 refers to Sima Yi (司馬懿), whose posthumous title was 宣王. The main text states 王廼具叙宣王創業之始 (Wang then narrated in detail the beginning of Xuan Wang's founding enterprise), and the Liu annotation confirms 宣王創業誅曹爽任蔣濟之流 (Xuan Wang's founding enterprise, executing Cao Shuang and employing Jiang Ji). None of the four candidates — 温嶠, 王導, 曹爽, or 蔣濟 — is Sima Yi. 温嶠 and 王導 are figures in the main text's narrative but not the referent of 宣王. 曹爽 and 蔣濟 are mentioned in the annotation as people involved in events during Xuan Wang's (Sima Yi's) enterprise, but they are not Xuan Wang himself. The correct referent, Sima Yi, is not among the supplied candidates.

The mention 桓景真 refers to Huan Liang (桓亮), whose courtesy name is 景真. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-19-xianyuan-032-liu-annotation-003) explicitly states 續晉陽秋曰桓亮字景真, confirming that 桓亮 (c8) is the person with courtesy name 景真. The main text (sfh1-ev-19-xianyuan-032-main) describes 繪之 encountering the 難 of 桓景真, and the annotation (sfh1-ev-19-xianyuan-032-liu-annotation-004) confirms 桓亮 killed 韓繪之. Candidates c2 (亮) and c6 (字景真) are components of the same identification but c8 (桓亮) is the full name form matching the referent.

The mention '伯倫' refers to Liu Ling (劉伶) via his courtesy name (字伯倫). The annotation text '名士傳曰伶字伯倫沛鄴' explicitly states that 伶 (Liu Ling) has the courtesy name 伯倫, directly linking the surface form to Liu Ling. Both candidates c0 and c1 refer to the same historical person Liu Ling. Candidate c1 is the existing person entity with richer corroborating evidence including the full biographical profile (劉伶字伯倫沛國人也...) and the annotation evidence, making it the preferred candidate. The main text '劉伶著酒徳頌' confirms the referent is Liu Ling.

The pronoun 朕 (imperial 'I') is spoken by the emperor who has just ascended the throne. The main text states 乃立康帝康帝登阼會群臣謂何曰朕今所以承大業... The speaker is 康帝 (Emperor Kang), who addresses the assembled ministers. The referent hint is 康帝, and candidate c0 is 康帝. The main text evidence (sfh1-ev-05-fangzheng-041-main) directly supports that 朕 refers to 康帝. All other candidates are different persons mentioned in the text or annotations (何充, 沈充, 潘岳, 世同, 京, 亮, 季, 平仲, 庾冰, 庾季堅, 庾氷, 氷) and are not the speaker of 朕.

The mention 仲文 refers to 殷仲文. The main text states '舊以桓謙比殷仲文' and then '桓玄時仲文入桓於庭中望見之', where 仲文 is the shortened personal name of 殷仲文, who was already introduced by full name in the same passage. Candidate c3 (殷仲文) is the correct referent. Candidates c0 (卞範之), c2 (桓謙), and c5 (謙) are contradicted by the evidence. Candidates c1 (仲文) and c4 (沖) are insufficiently grounded as distinct historical persons.

The mention '士龍' refers to 陸士龍 (陸雲). The main text lists '陸士衡士龍' together as brothers. Liu annotation 007 states '士龍吳大司馬抗之第五子機同母之弟也' and identifies 陸雲 as 字士龍. Annotation 009 confirms '陸士龍當今之顔淵'. Candidate c15 (陸雲) is the person whose 字 is 士龍. Candidate c14 (陸士龍) is the same person under a different name form. All other candidates are different people mentioned in the passage or annotations.

The mention 潁 refers to 王丞相's second younger brother 潁. The main text (sfh1-ev-09-pinzao-018-main) names him as 潁, and the Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-09-pinzao-018-liu-annotation-001) provides his courtesy name 茂英. Candidate c4 is the direct name 潁 matching the mention surface. Candidate c0 is the same person (潁/Ying) via semantic referent hint. Candidate c6 (茂英) is the courtesy name of the same person per the annotation. Candidates c1 (鄧伯道), c2 (敝), c3 (温忠武), and c5 (茂平) are different persons mentioned in the same passage.

The mention 孔廷尉 refers to 孔坦, who is explicitly named in the main text (sfh1-ev-05-fangzheng-037-main) as 孔坦. The office title 廷尉 combined with surname 孔 identifies the same person. The Liu annotations (sfh1-ev-05-fangzheng-037-liu-annotation-003, -004, -005) also refer to 坦/孔坦 in connection with this passage. Candidate c4 (孔坦) is the correct referent. Candidates c0 (王隱), c1 (蘇峻), c2 (陶侃) are other persons mentioned in the annotations but not the referent of 孔廷尉. Candidates c3 (坦), c5 (峻), c6 (石), c7 (碩) are partial-name candidates; c3 (坦) is a component of 孔坦's name and appears in annotations referring to the same person, but c4 is the full-name candidate explicitly identified in the main text.

The mention '亮' refers to 桓亮, whose courtesy name is 景真 (字景真) per Liu annotation 003. The annotation states 桓亮 is the grandson of 大司馬温 and son of 給事濟, and that he gathered troops at 長沙 styling himself 湘州刺史 (annotation 004). This matches 桓景真 in the main text who is the perpetrator of the 難 that killed 繪之. Candidate c7 (桓亮) and c8 (桓景真) both refer to the same person, but c7 is the direct referent of the surface '亮' as the personal name. The reference semantics explicitly identify 亮 as the personal name of 桓亮.

The mention 王丞相 refers to Wang Dao (王導), the Chancellor of the Eastern Jin court. The main text describes Wen Qiao visiting 王丞相 (Chancellor Wang), and the reference semantics explicitly identify the referent as 王導. Candidate c0 (王導) is the canonical registry match for this office title reference. Candidates c1 (劉琨) and c2 (温嶠) are other narrative participants in the same story but not the referent of 王丞相. Candidates c3 (管仲), c4 (管仲夷吾), and c5 (管夷吾) are historical figures from the Spring and Autumn period referenced in the text as a comparison (Wen Qiao says '江左自有管夷吾'), not the referent of 王丞相.

The mention 興公 is the courtesy name (字) of 孫綽. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-012-liu-annotation-001) explicitly identifies 太原孫綽, and the main text uses 興公 for the person who proposes marriage to 阿智. Candidate c0 (孫綽) and c3 (太原孫綽) both refer to the same person, with c0 being the direct name. The other candidates are different persons mentioned in the text or annotation (王文度, 䖍之/王䖍之, 文將, 阿恒, 阿智).

The mention 王大將軍 refers to 王敦. The main text uses 處仲 (王敦's courtesy name) in the same passage, and the Liu annotation explicitly states '王敦討劉隗時温太真', confirming 王大將軍 = 王敦. The other candidates are distinct persons mentioned in the text or annotations.

The mention '顧彦先' refers to 顧榮 (Gu Rong), whose courtesy name was 彦先. The external evidence (evidence-w3-person-b5d22d0f9f8eaefa796cc796) lists 顧彦先 among the Wu old families alongside 朱永長, 嚴仲弼, 張威伯, 陸士衡, 士龍 - matching the same list in the main text of this story. The other evidence (evidence-w3-person-0e11d449c8d6c66e93ee74cb, evidence-w3-person-0e2c0e1798f2b9c78a4d5d72) confirms 顧彦先 is 顧榮, a person known for playing the qin and associated with 陸平原 (陸機). All other candidates are different persons mentioned in the same passage or annotations.

The mention 王子敬 refers to the speaker in the main text, who addresses 王孝伯 (王恭). The candidates are 王恭 (c0) and 羊祜 (c1). 王恭 is the addressee (王孝伯), not the speaker 王子敬. 羊祜 (字叔子) is referenced in the text as 羊叔子, a third party being discussed, not the speaker. Neither candidate corresponds to 王子敬, who is a distinct person (王献之, courtesy name 子敬). The candidate set does not include the correct referent for 王子敬.

The mention 祖車騎 refers to 祖逖 by his office title 車騎將軍. The main text (sfh1-ev-08-shangyu-043-main) reads 劉琨稱祖車騎爲朗, where 祖車騎 combines the surname 祖 with the office title 車騎. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-08-shangyu-043-liu-annotation-008) confirms 贈車騎將軍 in connection with 逖's death, establishing that 車騎將軍 was 祖逖's posthumous office. The annotation (sfh1-ev-08-shangyu-043-liu-annotation-006) explicitly names 祖逖 in the narrative. Candidate c7 (祖逖) is the correct referent. Candidate c10 (逖) is a fragment of the same name and also supported, but c7 is the full name and preferred.

The mention '勒' refers to 石勒. Annotation-002 states '攸為石勒所獲' (攸 was captured by 石勒), establishing 石勒 as the full name. Annotation-004 states '勒知遣之' (勒 learned of it and sent someone), where '勒' is the same person as 石勒. The candidate c2 (石勒) is the correct referent. The other candidates (鄧攸, 攸, 綏, 遺民) are different persons in the narrative.

The mention '聘' refers to 謝聘, the younger brother of 謝奉, with courtesy name 弘. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-09-pinzao-040-liu-annotation-001) states '(氏譜曰奉弟聘字弘/安南謝奉也巳見謝)', directly identifying 聘 as 奉's younger brother with courtesy name 弘. Candidate c0 (謝聘) matches this referent directly. The other candidates are different persons: 儉 is 聘's father, 奉 is 聘's elder brother, 孔巖/巖/彭祖 refer to a different person (孔巖), 弘 is 聘's courtesy name (not the person himself), 逺 is a different person mentioned in annotation-002.

The mention '勒' refers to 石勒. Annotation-002 states '攸為石勒所獲' (攸 was captured by 石勒), establishing 石勒 as the full name. Annotation-004 states '勒知遣之' (勒 learned of it and sent someone), where '勒' is the same person as 石勒. The candidate c2 (石勒) is the correct referent. The other candidates (鄧攸, 攸, 綏, 遺民) are different persons in the narrative.

The mention 王丞相 refers to Wang Dao (王導), the Chancellor of the Eastern Jin court. The main text describes Wen Qiao visiting 王丞相 (Chancellor Wang), and the reference semantics explicitly identify the referent as 王導. Candidate c0 (王導) is the canonical registry match for this office title reference. Candidates c1 (劉琨) and c2 (温嶠) are other narrative participants in the same story but not the referent of 王丞相. Candidates c3 (管仲), c4 (管仲夷吾), and c5 (管夷吾) are historical figures from the Spring and Autumn period referenced in the text as a comparison (Wen Qiao says '江左自有管夷吾'), not the referent of 王丞相.

The mention 謝豫章 refers to Xie Kun (謝鯤), who held the office of Yuzhang (豫章) administrator. The main text states '謝仁祖年八嵗謝豫章將送客' — Xie Renzu (Xie Shang) at age 8, with Xie Yuzhang being his father. The Liu annotation-001 explicitly notes '(别見/鯤子)' identifying the subject as Kun's son, and annotation-002 states '人鯤之子也' (son of Kun). The reference semantics indicate this is an office-holder reference where 豫章 designates Xie Kun, who served as Yuzhang administrator. Candidate c0 (謝鯤) is the correct referent. Candidates c1 (温嶠), c3 (尚), c4 (嶠) appear in annotation-003 as different persons in the narrative about Xie Shang's mourning. Candidate c2 (謝尚) is the son, distinct from the father referenced by 謝豫章.
